House London #1 · Seat 67

The Replacement Gap

Why aren’t we tearing down old buildings?

London mostly extends in place. When we ask to replace, approval is comparable — the gap is volume, not refusal.

151,398 Foreman applications classified · R validation · GLA Datahub cross-check

The question

Demolition feels blocked — is it policy, or pipeline?

  • Hypothesis A: councils refuse demolition more than extensions.
  • Hypothesis B: we rarely submit replacement schemes in the first place.

We tested both on the full Foreman London extract using a reproducible keyword taxonomy and statistical validation in R.

Headline

The replacement gap is volume

6.3 : 1 extend-to-replace applications

107,502 extend vs 17,180 replace. We don’t fail at demolition — we rarely ask.

External check: GLA Planning London Datahub — 146k householder permissions vs 8.3k conservation-area demolition apps = 17.5 : 1 (same direction, official application types).

Approval rates

Replace ≈ extend once you ask

Point gap replace−extend: −2.6pp. Borough cluster bootstrap (B=500): 95% CI −6.3 to +2.8 pp — not significant.

Change-of-use is the hard path

Classifier validation

Taxonomy checked on a gold sample

CheckResult
Stratified sample400 apps (100 per category)
Legacy classifier vs gold rubric92.2% acc · macro-F1 0.92
Pass-2 blind re-label (80 rows)Cohen's κ = 0.883
Main error patternreplace → extend (accessory demolition)
Agent-applied gold rubric with independent pass-2 implementation — not a human panel, but reproducible and error-typed.

Statistical stack

What we ran (and where)

  • Wilson 95% CIs on 151k approval rates (analysis/validate_headline.R)
  • Borough cluster bootstrap (B=500) for extend vs replace gap
  • 3 decision-coding policies — gap stable under strict / current / permissive
  • Strict-replace sensitivity — explicit demolition regex subset (n=3,787, 55% approved)
  • PLD guest API — structured type counts (scripts/sample_pld.py)
Outputs: reference/validation.md · reference/classifier-validation.md · reference/pld-triangulation.md

Honesty

What we do not claim

  • Not ground-truth planning policy analysis — keyword taxonomy on free text
  • Not pro-demolition — describing application mix, not advocating teardown
  • Borough rankings are exploratory (no multiple-comparison correction)
  • Foreman structured fields (n_dwellings) are ~99% empty — not used for headline

Decision strings unknown: 2.5% of raw Foreman rows.
